THE ITEM-2 BLOCKING PROBE. Does the TRUNK carry absolute momentum, or only its inputs? Frozen 128-d representations, 400,000 jets, split 240k/80k/80k, ridge (alpha by CV) + 3-seed MLP + a 10-permutation null. RESULT ln jet_pt, ridge/MLP: L162 0.8029/0.9206, R16_Q1 0.8399/0.9241. |jet_eta|: L162 0.6054/0.8260, R16_Q1 0.5838/0.8073. NEGATIVE CONTROL signed jet_eta: -0.0004/-0.0013 and -0.0003/-0.0009, every permutation null -0.0004. THE PROBE IS TRUSTWORTHY AND THIS IS THE FIRST TIME THAT CAN BE SAID: both negative controls sit within 0.0001 of their own null, so the representation holds NO information about the sign of eta while holding a great deal about |eta| - the signature of a Delphes resolution table symmetric in eta and binned in |eta|. G-0's signed-eta 0.107 was the GBDT fitting summary statistics. Both spec conditions at audit/pt_recoverability_probe_spec.md:170-172 pass for both arms; G-0 never computed the null at all. THE TRUNK CARRIES MORE SCALE THAN THE INPUTS APPEARED TO: 0.582 at input level vs 0.92 at the representation - the direction implied by 0.582 being a LOWER bound (51 summary statistics, no relative-pT feature, so no per-track join; an attention trunk can form one). E1 GATE DID NOT PASS - and the defect is in the figure, not the model. Ran on the public Sophon features (E0b), 870,981 QCD jets in the 20<m_SD<500 window, signal = the ten 2P_HAD_2PARTON native labels with uniform alpha. chi2/ndf vs flat = 99.0 / 26.3 / 17.8 at eps_B = 0.05 / 0.01 / 0.005, ratio range 0.610-1.399 rising to 0.439-2.127; at eps_B=0.05 the lowest mass bin is 0.610 +/- 0.008, i.e. 48 sigma below unity, and the spectrum rises monotonically to ~1.4 by m~430 GeV. THE MECHANISM IS PRESENT: configs/data/JetClassII_base.yaml:149-152 sets reweight_method flat over jet_pt x jet_sdmass, so Sophon IS trained with the same 2D decorrelation GloParT uses - but the decorrelation holds AT FIXED pT on a FLAT-REWEIGHTED training distribution, and this figure was made INCLUSIVELY IN pT on the NATURAL falling test spectrum. ZERO GPU, CPU ONLY. Cross-domain flavour probe, run to answer an adversarial objection: is the QCD axis a third effect of a different kind, or the resonant flavour feature re-read on QCD jets? Fitted on the same cached features_v2 (2,000,000 jets, rows for label188 0/1/169/181), same SPLIT_SEED 20260822 and same C grid as probe.py. VALIDATION FIRST: the in-domain AUCs reproduce results.tex to 4-5 decimals (L162 0.99759 resonant, 0.98349 QCD; R16_Q1 s2/s3/s4 0.99268/0.98950/0.99105) and the per-seed contrasts to within 0.001, so this is also an independent re-derivation of the paper's headline table from raw features, which is what docs/REVIEW.md asks for. RESULT: one linear direction fitted on the UNION of both flavour axes, domain-balanced, reaches essentially in-domain AUC on each (L162 0.99700/0.98319 against 0.99755/0.98335 in-domain; every R16_Q1 seed likewise). The direction fitted on QCD jets ALONE - jets that carry no flavour label in either arm - separates resonant b from resonant c at 0.99519 in L162. The converse is weaker (0.96254), which is what near-separable data does to its own fit: the resonant axis at AUC 0.998 under-determines the direction. Cosine between the two per-domain directions in a COMMON standardised space is positive in every arm (L162 0.50-0.71, R16_Q1 0.50-0.88). DO NOT QUOTE the raw-space cosine (L162 -0.199): it is a per-domain-scaler artefact and is wrong. CONSEQUENCE: the paper claimed 'three effects of different size and different kind'. It is two - a general coarsening cost, and the loss of one erased feature measured in two domains. That reframing is weaker as a headline and stronger as evidence, because it rules out the reading that L162 merely memorised a head-adjacent split between two of its own training labels. DP-2026-104 Fig. 7 is p_T-binned. Threshold set per p_T bin on that bin's own QCD jets; bins with <500 selected at a working point are flagged THIN and excluded from the gate. A synthetic test (two p_T populations, D a function of p_T only) sculpts inclusively and is flat per bin, so the diagnosis is encoded as a test that must pass. THIS IS THE GATE FOR THE MASS-REGRESSION PAPER: if the binned ratio is flat the pipeline reproduces the published discriminant behaviour and E2/E3/E3b may proceed; if it is not flat the discriminant itself sculpts m_SD and the direction stops. Inclusive result kept at /data/results/massreg/e1_control; this writes e1_control_pt. RESULT 2026-09-05: THE DIAGNOSIS WAS WRONG. Binning in p_T does NOT remove the sculpting. chi2/ndf vs flat at eps_B=0.05/0.01/0.005: [200,400) 9.9/6.3/2.4; [400,600) 20.4/1.5/2.6; [600,1000) 121.5/52.6/68.0; [1000,1500) 41.2/7.9/4.5; [1500,2500) 34.2/7.0/4.0. The 20-500 window is entirely inside the reweighting range (jet_sdmass edges 20..500, jet_pt 200..2500), so 'outside the flat region' is excluded. Remaining candidate before the model is blamed: the DISCRIMINANT. Uniform alpha over all ten 2P_HAD_2PARTON labels includes X_qq/X_gg/X_ss, and a QCD jet at high m/pT is kinematically a light two-prong object, so a cut on 'light two-prong resonance' must select high-mass QCD; the published figure is for a flavour-tagged signal whose discriminant rides on impact parameters. Next: rerun per signal set (X_bb alone, X_qq alone, the deployed 2-prong S with alpha=2 on qq). Until that runs, E1 is FAILED and nothing downstream in docs/MASSREG_EXPERIMENTS.md may proceed.

READ 2409.12589 IN FULL BEFORE IMPLEMENTING, AND IT CORRECTED MY OWN RECORDED RECIPE IN TWO PLACES. Item 17 and the decision-17 ledger row recorded 'transformer decoder, 40 % mask, particle-ID head, full 17-feature input'. Reading the paper: (1) MPMv2 is MAE-STYLE -- masked particles are REMOVED from the encoder input and reintroduced only at the decoder, not replaced in place ('significantly more efficient to remove all masked tokens from the input set and reintroduce them only during decoding ... a departure of a model similar to BERT to a model more akin to MAE'). I had not recorded this at all, and it is the source of the paper's 40 percent memory saving. (2) NO BACKBONE IS TRAINED ON PARTICLE-ID ALONE: section 5.2 states every evaluated backbone pairs ID with one continuous-feature task. An ID-only objective would have been one the paper never measures, so a weak result could not have been read against the published numbers -- exactly the ambiguity the pre-registered validity bar exists to remove, defeated before the first run. (3) 30 percent is the ablation mask rate (Table 1 caption); 40 percent is right but only for the final tuned config. TASK CHOSEN: Regression + ID. The whole spread across pretrained backbones at 100M jets is 85.0 (regression) to 85.3 (K-Means) against a random-init baseline of 84.3, so the gap between the best task and the simplest is 0.3 points -- inside our own per-epoch validation SD of 0.047-0.075 and therefore unmeasurable here. Regression additionally WINS the weakly-supervised CWoLa setting (SIC 8.18) and adds no extra training stage, where K-Means needs a 16,384-centroid fit over 1M jets and VQVAE needs a separately trained unstable model. DELIBERATE DEVIATION: we do NOT add MPMv2's 8 encoder registers (worth +1.2/+1.6 accuracy) because a register changes the trunk and I5 fixes the architecture across arms; with registers the SSL arm would differ from the supervised arms in two things at once and stop being a clean denominator. Recorded so the paper states it rather than a referee finding it. Note research/notes/mpmv2-recipe-corrected-2026-09-07.md; item 17 recipe paragraph rewritten in place.

MPM arm implemented, ZERO GPU consumed, which is the point -- item 17 sequenced the code into the GPU-starved window. experiments/MTX/mpm.py (348 lines) and experiments/MTX/ParT_sophon_arch_mpm.py follow the hybrid_mass.py precedent exactly: the image ships released weaver 0.4.17 with no SSL train mode and no get_train_fn hook, weaver.train._main imports train_classification INSIDE the function, so install() replacing it before main() is what runs. The arch REFUSES to build unless the loop is installed, the same guard the mass arch carries, because weaver's stock loop would otherwise train silently against a label this objective never uses. DESIGN CHOICE WORTH THE PAPER: masking is applied through the ATTENTION MASK rather than by compacting the tensor. Zeroing a particle's mask bit removes it from every attention computation as a key and zeroes its embedding, so the encoder output at surviving positions is IDENTICAL to what true removal gives; what is given up is only MPMv2's 40 percent memory saving, not the objective, and in exchange the trunk is called through the same embed/blocks modules the supervised arms use with no gather/scatter that could silently reorder an unordered set. Memory is not binding (the arms already fit at 14.8 GB and the decoder is quarter width). Encoder forward is replicated from weaver 0.4.17 verbatim up to the end of blocks because 0.4.17 exposes no encoder/aggregator split -- the same measurement E1's arch file already records -- and is commented to stay in sync. The 17 pf_features split as 11 continuous (L1) and 6 categorical that reduce to exactly 8 type+charge classes (CE), which is coincidentally the same 8 MPMv2 uses. MEASURED THE ONE CONVENTION THAT COULD HAVE SILENTLY RUINED EVERY DOWNSTREAM ROW. part_deta and part_dphi are RAW branches in both JetClass-I and JetClass-II -- no config in this repo derives them (checked: the only occurrence outside an inputs: slot is part_deltaR = np.hypot(part_deta, part_dphi)) -- so any converter for a new dataset has to reproduce whatever the dataset authors did, and a wrong convention is SILENT: the model trains, the loss falls, and every top/qg number is quietly degraded. Rather than recall it, measured on 100,000 real jets of /jc2/jet_data/QCD_0000.parquet by recomputing eta and phi from part_px/py/pz and comparing four candidates against the released branch (float32 agreement is ~5e-07): part_deta = (part_eta - jet_eta) * sign(jet_eta) agrees to 4.8e-07 and is CORRECT, while the unflipped part_eta - jet_eta is off by 6.44; part_dphi = wrap(part_phi - jet_phi) agrees to 4.2e-07 and is CORRECT, while the sign-flipped version is off by 2.18. THE SIGN FLIP IS APPLIED TO ETA AND NOT TO PHI. That asymmetry is not guessable and both wrong answers are the natural guesses. CONSEQUENCE ENCODED IN THE CONVERTER: the flip needs a meaningful sign(jet_eta), so a source that ships constituents already centred on the jet axis would have ~half its jets mirrored at random; scripts/stage_downstream.py measures median |jet_eta| per split and REFUSES to write below 0.05 rather than producing a silently mirrored sample.

THE ZERO-FILL AND ITS CONTROL NOW COME FROM ONE DECLARATION, WHICH IS THE ONLY WAY THE CONTROL IS EVIDENCE. PRD_PLAN 4.5 / item 16d approve zero-filling what the top set (10 of 17 features: charge, 5 PID flags, 4 displacement) and EnergyFlow q/g (4: d0, d0err, dz, dzerr) do not carry, CONDITIONAL on masking the same features on JetClass-II and showing the arm ordering survives. HOW THE FILL IS APPLIED: not by redefining the absent branch (weaver new_variables shadowing a real branch is undefined, and on the CONTROL the branch does exist) but by defining part_zero = ak.zeros_like(part_energy) once and pointing each filled slot at it WHILE KEEPING THE ARMS' STANDARDIZATION PARAMETERS -- which matters because the d0err/dzerr slots are [.., 0, 1, 0, 1] and the PID slots are [.., null], and a raw 0 maps to a network input of 0 under every one of them, so keeping the parameters changes nothing numerically and holds the diff to the variable name. tests/test_downstream_fill.py, 12 tests, re-derives the masked slot sets from the EMITTED YAML rather than the generator's table and asserts they are equal, that the control differs from configs/arms/L162.yaml ONLY in the declared slots, that the generator's FEATURES list still matches the arm config, that every filled slot's transform really maps 0 to 0, and that no downstream config still references an absent branch (a leftover part_d0: np.tanh(part_d0val) in the top config would crash the loader on the first batch, after staging, after scheduling, on a GPU). Suite 225 passed, 1 skipped. HONEST LIMIT RECORDED IN THE FILES: the control bounds the penalty and shows whether the ORDERING survives masking in-domain; it does NOT prove the ordering survives on the top set's own distribution, and nothing short of reduced-feature pretraining per target (~84 GPU-days, ParT's route) would. That is the stated limitation, not a gap the control quietly covers.

FOUR DEFECTS CAUGHT, each of which had a silent failure mode. (2) A single shared part_zero variable is REFUSED by weaver: it keys standardization by variable NAME and our filled slots carry two different transforms (PID slots null, d0err/dzerr [0,1,0,1]). Fixed with one zero variable per replaced feature (part_zero_d0err etc.), which is strictly better -- each slot keeps the arms' own standardization so the fill stays numerically identical, and the name records what it stands in for. DECIDED THE FINE-TUNING LR QUESTION AND MEASURED IT INSTEAD OF ASSUMING (PI: 'You determine what to do'). THE GAP: docs/GATES.md G1 settled the equivalent question for PRETRAINING by measurement -- 5e-4 is R16_Q1's outright argmax and ties L162's, gap 0.00316, a fifth of the margin -- and G1's kill condition is explicit, 'if the optimum moves with K, a single LR confounds granularity with tuning, and every arm needs its own LR sweep'. NOTHING EQUIVALENT HAS EVER BEEN MEASURED AT FINE-TUNING; the legs use 1e-4 because it is ParT's published value, inherited. WHY THAT IS NOT A SMALL RISK: if a coarse arm needs a different FT rate than a fine one, the handicap is CORRELATED WITH THE QUANTITY UNDER STUDY, so we would read 'coarse vocabulary transfers worse' when part of the gap is 'coarse vocabulary needs more adaptation' -- bias in the direction of our own hypothesis, not noise. LITERATURE CHECKED AND IT IS GENUINELY SPLIT: Ranking Neural Checkpoints (CVPR 2021), the canonical checkpoint-comparison paper, sweeps hyper-parameters PER checkpoint-task pair and keeps the best; LP-FT (Kumar et al., ICLR 2022) sweeps 3 LRs and states it 'checked that the best learning rate was not at the boundary of the grid search'; HEP practice (ParT, MIParT) reports one rate and never sweeps per variant. Ranking Neural Checkpoints is measuring best-achievable-per-checkpoint, a DIFFERENT estimand from ours -- our claim is about what a vocabulary preserves, and I1 requires arms to differ in exactly one thing, so per-arm optima would weaken the claim to 'arm A at its optimum beats arm B at its optimum'. DECISION: headline stays the MATCHED protocol, and the probe measures whether that is defensible rather than assuming it. If the optimum does not move with K, the paper says so with data instead of by inheritance; if it does move, we report each arm at its own optimum BESIDE the matched protocol and the shift itself becomes a finding, because coarser vocabularies needing more adaptation is a real result. Recorded as DECISIONS_PENDING item 20 (YELLOW).

An optimum at a grid boundary is not an optimum -- LP-FT states the check explicitly ('checked that the best learning rate was not at the boundary of the grid search') -- and a near-certain loser BELOW 5e-4 is precisely what brackets it from below, so the point is worth buying after all. Nested subsets for the two published benchmarks at tag mtx-s1.12. TWO CORRECTIONS I MADE TO MY OWN FIRST VERSION, both from reading docs/PRD_PLAN.md 4.1 rather than the item-16 summary line. (1) PER-DATASET N_max: top {1e3,1e4,1e5,1.2e6} (2606.14870's grid), q/g {1e3,1e4,1e5,1.6e6} (its whole chunk-aligned training split). I had flattened both to 1e6, which would have quietly retired the top end of both community tables. (2) The ParT recipe's 5e-3 is the HEAD rate in a discriminative-LR scheme (1e-4 trunk / 5e-3 head = 50x, exactly weaver's lr_mult multiplier), NOT the scratch rate; scratch is 5e-4. MEASURED DEFECT THIS JOB EXISTS TO FIX: top_train stores rows in BLOCKS OF 10 sharing a label (every run length a multiple of 10, longest 180), so a contiguous window's class fraction is sqrt(10) noisier than an iid draw -- measured inflation 3.01x at N=1e3 and 3.12x at N=1e4 against sqrt(10)=3.16, and the first 1,000 rows are 46.0% top. The N=1e3 cell that PRD_PLAN 4.1 adds is exactly the cell that skew would have damaged most. make_subsets bench routes both sets through the per-seed shuffle and hard-fails if any subset's signal fraction drifts past 0.05. Memory 64Gi, not 48Gi: q/g N_max is the whole 1.6M pool and the shuffle COPIES it, so the peak is about twice the pool. VERIFIED 2026-09-07 after the job succeeded in ~150s (top_sub 5.1G, qg_sub 11G): all 24 emitted files re-read from the PVC -- 3 seeds x 4 sizes per dataset with exact row counts and every signal fraction inside 0.05 of parity, the nesting property held at EVERY consecutive pair, not just the first -- 1e3 in 1e4 in 1e5 in 1.2e6 for top and 1e3 in 1e4 in 1e5 in 1.6e6 for q/g, each checked as a literal array prefix, which is the property a data-scaling curve depends on (a larger budget strictly adds data), N_max is each set's own split (top 1.2e6, q/g 1.6e6), and both validation files are 200,000 jets at 0.4992 (top) and 0.5000 (q/g). The exit code was not taken as proof. ONE PROPERTY WORTH STATING RATHER THAN DISCOVERING LATER: at N_max NEITHER dataset's three files are independent draws: the q/g trio holds the SAME 1.6M jets in three orders, and top's 1.2M is drawn from a 1,211,000-row split so any two seeds share 99.1% of their jets. The caveat was recorded only for q/g, which implied top's N_max cell was a genuine sampling error bar. It is not; at N_max both are shuffle-order spread, because N_max IS the whole training split -- so the seed spread at N_max measures head init, dropout and order, NOT data sampling. THE FIRST LABELREC RUN'S MLP COLUMN WAS AN OPTIMISATION FAILURE, NOT A MEASUREMENT, AND NOTHING RECORDED IT. MLPClassifier(hidden_layer_sizes=(512,), max_iter=300) with early_stopping defaulting to False hit the iteration cap on every cell -- sklearn raised ConvergenceWarning throughout -- and l162-s1b on L188 returned mlp 0.2813 against linear 0.3454 (chance 0.0053). An MLP cannot be worse than a linear probe once converged: its hypothesis class CONTAINS the linear one. THIS IS PRECISELY THE INFERENCE D6 EXISTS TO PREVENT: a linear probe only lower-bounds mutual information, so the nonlinear probe is mandatory beside any null to tell 'absent' from 'present but not linearly decodable' -- and that argument is void if the MLP simply ran out of iterations. The output had no field from which a reader could tell. FIXED: early_stopping=True with n_iter_no_change=15, ceiling raised to 1000, and mlp_n_iter / mlp_converged / mlp_below_linear carried into every cell. The SAME blind spot was checked in probe.py, the PRIMARY D6 probe: its hand-written torch loop already does patience-8 early stopping with best-state restore and is sound, but it could not distinguish 'plateaued' from 'ran out of epochs' either, so epochs_run / converged / all_converged were added there too. Independent confirmation the fix works: the suite's warning count fell 29 -> 8 as the ConvergenceWarnings disappeared. The running job was killed rather than allowed to finish -- its MLP column would have been unusable and the fixed version is also faster. Relaunched at mtx-s1.31. 412 tests pass.

THE BRACKETING PROBE LANDED AND IT SETTLES ITEM 22 AGAINST THE ITEM'S OWN ASSUMPTION. All six cells ran after the relaunch. r16q1-s2: 3e-3 0.93074, 1e-2 0.93033, 3e-2 0.93039. l162-s1b: 3e-3 0.92844, 1e-2 0.93006, 3e-2 0.93045. THE OVERLAP ANCHOR REPRODUCED EXACTLY: lrprobe2's 3e-3 cells were 0.93074 and 0.92844, identical to five decimals in both arms, so variance at fixed seed is nil and the curve can be read as one measurement. Full curve, r16q1-s2 then l162-s1b, at 3e-5/1e-4/3e-4/1e-3/3e-3/1e-2/3e-2: 0.89285 0.90279 0.91576 0.92643 0.93074 0.93033 0.93039 and 0.89320 0.90461 0.91703 0.92553 0.92844 0.93006 0.93045. TWO CONCLUSIONS. (1) The optimum is a PLATEAU from 3e-3 to 3e-2 at about 0.930-0.931, not a peak. (2) Item 22 said the 1e-4 handicap 'biases the absolute numbers rather than the ordering'. FALSE. At 1e-4 l162 leads by 0.00182; at 3e-3 r16q1 leads by 0.00230; at 3e-2 they are level within 0.00006. On top tagging the arms are indistinguishable once both are properly tuned, and the gap visible at the pre-registered rate is a LEARNING-RATE ARTEFACT, not a vocabulary effect. A second wave at 1e-4 would therefore produce a biased arm comparison. CONSTRAINT ON THE FIX: the per-arm argmax differs (3e-3 for r16q1, 3e-2 for l162), so tuning per arm introduces a second variable and violates I1. One shared rate is required; 1e-2 puts both within 0.0005 of their own peak with a 0.00027 gap and is the least-bad single choice. This is top tagging at one fine-tuning seed on one pretraining seed per arm -- it bounds the confound, it is not the transfer headline.

THE NODE EXCLUSIONS WERE NEVER ON THE CLUSTER, AND THE ARM I EXCLUDED A NODE FOR LANDED ON IT ANYWAY. THE EDIT WAS COSMETIC FOR EVERY JOB ALREADY CREATED: a Job's spec.template is immutable, so editing the local YAML changes nothing on-cluster and there is no patch path for nodeAffinity. Verified directly -- local job-mtx-l188-s1-raunav.yaml carried 6 exclusions while the cluster Job carried 4, MISSING exactly the two I had added. So when mtx-l188-s1 escaped a 4h12m Pending stretch it scheduled straight onto nrp-fiona-001, the node the edit existed to avoid; attempts.log shows it had already been placed on bad nodes twice before (nautilus-ext-gpu01, then nrp-fiona-001 on 2026-09-09). At 2.59 h/epoch with 59 epochs left it was the whole wave's critical path at 6.4 days. FIX: delete + recreate, the only way to change a Job's node affinity. PRE-FLIGHT BEFORE DELETING, because a delete with a broken resume loses 20 epochs: (1) epoch 20 has BOTH net_epoch-20_state.pt and net_epoch-20_optimizer.pt -- the auto-resume guard requires the pair, since weaver writes them separately and resuming from a state file with no optimizer only WARNS and then trains on with a fresh optimizer, silently corrupting a momentum-based run; (2) the on-disk RECIPE stamp is 'lr=5e-4 epochs=80' and the spec's is identical, so the recipe guard passes -- node affinity is not part of the stamp, so the exclusion edit cannot break resume; (3) the container args are BYTE-IDENTICAL between the cluster Job and the local spec (md5 1aabbedd7ce652a81685f2a7eab45926), same image, same 76Gi/4cpu/1gpu, same backoffLimit 50 -- so the recreate changes the excluded-node list and nothing else. Checkpoints re-verified intact AFTER the delete: 21 files, highest epoch 20, pair present, RECIPE unchanged. Recreated with all 6 exclusions confirmed live on the new Job. EXPECTED VALUE: 59 x 2.59 = 153h becomes 59 x ~1.25 = 74h, saving ~3.3 days, and the wave's critical path drops to mtx-r42q1-s3 at 5.7 days. RISK ACCEPTED KNOWINGLY: the pod requests 76Gi AND a 3090, a narrow intersection that cost 4h12m of Pending last time, and the new job went Pending immediately. knuron was deliberately NOT added to this arm's exclusion list: the evidence is now mixed (mtx-rand-d1-s1b is on knuron at 1.46 h/epoch, only ~19% above healthy) and narrowing an already-narrow placement further trades a certain queue cost for an uncertain throughput gain. Same reason nautilus-ext-gpu01 stays excluded only because it already was -- mtx-l188-s2 is on it right now at 1.24 h/epoch, i.e. fine. Editing a spec file does not move a running job.

BOTH FINE-TUNING LEGS READ OUT FROM net_best_epoch_state.pt, THE SELECTION RULE ITEM 18 RULED AGAINST FOR PRETRAINING -- CHECKED RATHER THAN ASSUMED, AND THE HEADLINE SURVIVES. leg1's extract_manifest.json names checkpoint .../net_best_epoch_state.pt and leg2's predict.log/stdout.log load the same, so the transfer table rests on weaver's best-validation-epoch marker. Item 18 resolved the PRETRAINING checkpoint to epoch 79 uniformly because that marker selects on which validation files were drawn rather than on the model: per-epoch SD 0.047-0.075 with 4-11 epochs tied inside 0.02 of the maximum. Taking a max over tied noisy epochs is an UPWARD-BIASED estimate, and the bias grows with validation noise -- which is largest at N=1e4, exactly where the biggest effects were reported. So the concern is real and had to be sized. MEASURED FROM THE EXISTING LOGS, ZERO COMPUTE, ALL 54 leg2 CELLS WITH A FULL CURVE: best-minus-last validation metric has median 0.00023, mean 0.00046, 90th percentile 0.00097, max 0.00373. The best epoch IS the last in 17/54 cells and within two of the end in 32/54. WHY FINE-TUNING DIFFERS FROM PRETRAINING HERE, which is the substantive point: the FT curves are short (10 epochs) and still converging, so 'best' is essentially 'last' and the selection wobble is ~100x smaller than the pretraining case item 18 was written about (0.0002-0.001 vs 0.02-0.075). Item 18's mechanism applies in principle but is negligible in magnitude here. WHAT SURVIVES AND WHAT DOES NOT. The granularity result is safe by 16-124x: L162 over the r16q1 mean is +0.062 / +0.010 / +0.008 at N=1e4/1e5/1e6 against a typical selection wobble of 0.0005. NOT SAFE as a ranking: L162 over sophon-public at N=1e6 is +0.0007, comparable to the wobble and smaller than its 90th percentile -- that pair must be reported as a TIE, which is how it was already stated (inside SD), and must never be upgraded to 'L162 beats the public checkpoint' at large N. The +0.059 gap over sophon-public at N=1e4 is safe. NO RERUN NEEDED. Re-reading out from the last epoch would cost inference over 108 cells to move numbers by ~0.0002, which is below every effect being claimed.

THE IN-DOMAIN LEG WAS NEVER READ OUT. job-ft-legs finished 108/108 fine-tunes, but only leg 2 had a metric: weaver prints a Test metric into each leg-2 predict.log, so that table came straight out of the logs. Leg 1 fine-tunes JetClass-II's OWN 162-way vocabulary and writes a feature cache instead -- features.npy, logits.npy, label188.npy per cell -- and a grep for leg1 across every .py in the repo returned only the job builder and its test. 54 cells, ~70 GB of finished inference, unread since the wave completed. Without it the transfer claim is half-measured: leg 2 shows the granularity effect under DOMAIN SHIFT, and leg 1 is the in-domain control on the same grid. An effect that appeared only under shift would mean something different from one that appears in both. experiments/FT/leg1_metrics.py + 7 tests, tag mtx-s1.35. METRICS ARE REUSED, NOT REDEFINED: accuracy / macro_auc_ovr / per-class AUC come from eval_arm.metrics(), the function the E1 gate was measured with, and the 188->L162 mapping from label_recovery.rung_maps() reading the committed map. Two definitions of one quantity is how two of this project's own tables stop being comparable. L162 group 161 is asserted at runtime to hold exactly the 27 QCD classes, because the QCD id is hard-coded for the rejection metric and a remap would otherwise compute it against a resonant class. THE AUC IS ON A STRIDE AND THE ACCURACY IS NOT. Accuracy is an argmax and free at 2Mx162; macro OvR AUC is 162 ROC curves over 2M rows and metrics() also does per-class, so a full pass is ~2x162 sorts per cell across 54 cells. --auc-stride 4 is DETERMINISTIC (no seed to record), takes the SAME rows in every cell so the between-init contrast stays paired instead of carrying per-cell sampling noise, and preserves the class mix, which a head slice would not -- the test list interleaves Res2P/Res34P/QCD by file. TWO DEFECTS THE TESTS CAUGHT BEFORE LAUNCH, both mine. (1) The label lookup table was sized from the map alone, so a native label beyond it raised a raw numpy IndexError instead of the named failure -- the same class of defect as letting it through, since neither tells the reader that cache and map disagree. Now sized from both and negatives rejected. (2) An end-to-end run against the REAL committed map was added rather than only unit tests, and it is what proved the module-loading path (exec_module of eval_arm and label_recovery) actually works outside pytest. Row alignment is a hard gate: the sha256 of label188.npy is compared across all 54 cells and a mismatch exits non-zero rather than averaging cells that scored different jets -- the failure that would otherwise produce a clean-looking table with no error at all. Observed rate ~76 s/cell, so ~1 h for the grid.

THE ANOMALY MODULE REBUILT AS ONE JOB PER ARM, AND TWO STALE LEDGER CLAIMS CORRECTED. FIRST, THE CORRECTION: the audit-2-anomaly row says the module 'must not be run' because sigma_min was the Gaussian estimator arXiv:2604.20965 refuses and the k-NN template was scored against itself. BOTH ARE ALREADY FIXED AND WIRED IN -- anomaly.py line 415 sets rec['sigma_min'] = sigma_min_asimov(...) with the Gaussian kept only as a secondary field, and line 366 uses score_knn_selfless(Xt). That row is stale and the module's science defects are closed. Checked rather than assumed, because acting on it would have meant rewriting code that was already correct. WHAT WAS ACTUALLY OPEN IS STRUCTURAL. The single-process run died after ~25 h with ONE arm of four finished and the pod was garbage-collected before it could be inspected, so the cause was never determined. A run whose failure mode cannot be diagnosed must not also be a run whose failure costs everything. Arms are independent up to one final normalisation, so each is now its own job: a death costs ONE arm; the arms run in PARALLEL so wall clock is one arm (~25 h) not four; and l162-s1b, which completed 2026-09-09, is NOT re-run -- its artifact is merged in as-is, saving ~25 h. Three arms launched, not four. THE TRAP IN SPLITTING BY ARM, AND WHY THE MERGE IS A PROGRAM AND NOT A `cat`. The regret the ablation is about is sigma_min / min over ARMS at fixed (signal, N_sig, family). An arm run alone takes that minimum over ITSELF and writes regret 1.000 for every family -- 'no regret from coarsening the vocabulary', the null under test, manufactured by the aggregation. That is precisely the defect audit-2-anomaly found when the normalisation sat inside the arm loop, and splitting arms across jobs REINTRODUCES it unless something recomputes. So cross_arm_regret() and null_guard() were extracted from anomaly.main() verbatim and anomaly_merge.py CALLS THEM rather than reimplementing the arithmetic; the per-arm regret fields are stale by construction and are overwritten. Each per-arm spec says in its own header that its regret column must not be read. The merge refuses inputs disagreeing on row_alignment_sha256, trainings, n_bkg, n_template, stat_cut, min_bkg_pass or sigma_t, so reusing the older l162-s1b artifact cannot silently mix incommensurable cells, and it refuses a DUPLICATED arm rather than last-one-wins, which would hide which run a published number came from. Output goes to anomaly_merged; /data/results/eval/anomaly is an INPUT and is never overwritten. anomaly_merge.py + 7 tests; 22 existing anomaly tests still pass after the extraction. Tag mtx-s1.36.

Macro OvR AUC on an every-4th-row stride tracks accuracy throughout (l162 0.920/0.978/0.980 vs r16q1 0.863-0.879/0.972/0.977). THE GRANULARITY EFFECT IS NOT A DOMAIN-SHIFT ARTEFACT. L162 over the r16q1 mean, in units of the r16q1 PRETRAINING-seed SD: leg 1 +0.0848 (8.7 SD) / +0.0401 (23.7) / +0.0246 (29.6); leg 2 +0.0621 (13.1) / +0.0100 (27.7) / +0.0077 (44.5). Same sign, same monotone narrowing with N, and LARGER in-domain -- as expected, since leg 1 asks the model to reproduce the very vocabulary L162 was pretrained on. An effect visible only under domain shift would have meant something quite different; it is visible in both. L162 TIES THE PUBLIC SOPHON CHECKPOINT AT LARGE N IN BOTH LEGS, TO REMARKABLE PRECISION: +0.0006 (leg 1) and +0.0007 (leg 2) at N=1e6. Both are inside the best-epoch selection wobble (median 0.00023, 90th pct 0.00097) and must be reported as ties in both legs. At small N the picture differs by leg: leg 2 +0.0587, leg 1 +0.1066. A CONFOUND THAT MUST NOT BE PUBLISHED AS A RESULT. At N=1e4 in leg 1, SCRATCH (0.31369) BEATS r16q1 (0.227-0.245) AND sophon-public (0.21613), and L162 edges it by only +0.0090. Read naively that says pretraining HURTS in-domain low-data transfer. It is a learning-rate confound: weaver's config dump shows start_lr 5e-4 for scratch and 1e-4 for every pretrained init, a 5x difference, at 50 epochs for all. That is the documented recipe (PRD_PLAN 4.1, 'LR 1e-4 pretrained / 5e-4 scratch'), so it is deliberate -- but it means the pretrained-vs-scratch contrast at N=1e4 varies TWO things at once and violates I1 for that contrast specifically. It corroborates item 22 / ft-lrprobe3, which found 1e-4 sits below the plateau and recommended one shared rate (1e-2) for wave 2: at 1e-4 the pretrained inits are simply under-trained at small N, and only L162's better starting point keeps it ahead of scratch at all. WHAT IS UNAFFECTED, AND IS THE PAPER'S CLAIM: the GRANULARITY contrast L162-vs-R16_Q1 uses 1e-4 on BOTH sides, so I1 holds for it and every figure above stands. Only the pretrained-vs-scratch column at N=1e4 is compromised, and it is compromised in both legs' small-N column by the same mechanism.
